questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I came for the challenge - and of course also culture and academic

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Something completely different and a recognized university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Really big challenge but also just what i wanted.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Terrible. The information is arbitrary and sometimes wrongful. Extremely tough start to figure out their system and getting the correct courses.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a tutor "Linda" but it was not always helpful. Often it was better to show up physically at the given office for your dilemma.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Very cheap but extremely worn 8-9 sqm bedroom and/or better (still cheap) 15-20 sqm bedrooms w own toilet.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Usually you eat in the canteens 2-3 times pr day, very cheap.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The process of getting a room is a first come first serve principle. No chance of getting any rooms or upgrades afterwards.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very chaotic.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Chinese old website with first come first serve - no courses guaranteed beforehand.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You had your supervisor and the other (many) exchange students. Most efficient to just go to the office of the given institute.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to get the courses i wanted after a lot of patience, stress and will.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will need to be very clear about what you want and not be scared to write mails.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Interesting courses and good professors. But very chinese view, as expected.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Good level, not that much homework (loads of time to explore china).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Smaller classes, high school vibes. Participation as a part of the grade in many courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: China's Regional and Global Engagement, Approach to Time Series Analysis, China's Globalization, Economic History

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Good course overall but be aware that everything with math is usually very theoretical and heavy on proves. 
The course about china (China's Regional and Global Engagement / China's Globalization) are really good and also easy, very much just about how much energy you want to put into it. I learned a lot.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not much

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didnt participate in many, but loads of different clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of things you can imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go travel!! Take the trains to everywhere, skip some classes!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Big culture chock, but very fun.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really, they were pretty much for themselfes unfortunately. Say hi to them in classes and/or join the clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Food culture (not eating very well behaved in danish standards).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Just the overall difference and chinese take on everything.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be ready for a challenge, travel a lot (amazing and diverse country), eat all the food.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many of other exchange students, dont worry about that part.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Growing as a person, meeting loads of nationalities, traveling and seeing so much different culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Course registration and communication with the administrative parts of Fudan.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
